lines: Stereo distortion modelled on a guitar pedal's diode clipper, with a filter that sweeps from dark to bright and a dry/wet mix
Runs the signal through the distortion when on; with it off the module is bypassed, and the switch crossfades between the two rather than stepping
Sweeps a filter from lowpass through mid-cut to highpass, taking the sound from darker to brighter; the readout runs 0 to 11
Sets the gain into the diode clipper, so turning it up squares the signal off harder; the clipping is soft rather than hard, despite the panel printing DIST
Sets how much of the distorted signal is in the output against the dry input, 0 to 100% wet
Sets the output gain
Adds to the TONE knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the DIST knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the MIX knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the LEVEL knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
The left audio input into the distortion
The right audio input into the distortion
The left output, carrying the dry signal and the distortion in the proportion set by MIX
The right output, carrying the dry signal and the distortion in the proportion set by MIX
Note — the two channels are separate circuits and neither input is normalled to the other, so with nothing patched into IN II the OUT II jack stays at 0V
Note — the circuit is modelled around a signal of ±1, and the module divides each input by 5 and multiplies each output by 5 to suit it, so ±5V is the level it expects

Blamsoft-XFXGrunge.notes: Blamsoft publish no source. Read from the installed 2.0.2 binary: the module class is DC1Module, its constructor at 0x25f8 and process at 0x1e88. configParam gives Enable 0 to 1 default 1 with an EnableParamQuantity printing Off and On, Tone 0 to 1 default 0.5 shown as 0 to 11, Distortion 0 to 1 default 0.5 shown as 0 to 11, Mix 0 to 1 default 1 shown as 0 to 100%, Level 0 to 1 default 0.75 shown as 0 to 11. Each CV jack is added to its knob at 0.1 per volt and the sum clamped to the knob's own 0 to 1 range, so a CV cannot push a control past its ends. The panel art draws a line from each jack to the knob it feeds and the disassembly agrees with every one. Enable does not use Rack's bypass: it selects between two modes of the generated DSP, the active circuit and a delay line that matches the active path's latency, and the module runs both in parallel for a short crossfade whenever the switch changes. The maker's PDF manual was read on this pass with pypdf; it agrees throughout and is the source of the account of what the Tone filter does. The widget adds no context menu of its own. The 2.0.2 binary is the only published build of this plugin, so no commit had to be settled.

Blamsoft-XFXTube.notes: Blamsoft publish no source. Read from the installed 2.0.2 binary: the module class is t00bModule, its constructor at 0xaf2c and process at 0xa7e4. config declares 10 parameters, 5 inputs, 2 outputs and no lights. Three of the ten parameters are two-position switches rather than knobs, which the panel does not make obvious: Tone and Extra Bass are configured with an EnableParamQuantity printing Off and On, Tone defaulting on and Extra Bass defaulting off. Model is 0 to 3 with a ModelParamQuantity printing A, B, C and D. Bass, Mid and Treble are each 0 to 1 with a display multiplier of 22 and an offset of -11, so they read -11 to +11 and centre at 0. Distortion and Level read 0 to 11, Mix 0 to 100%. Only Distortion, Mix and Level have CV jacks. Changing Enable, Tone, Extra Bass or Model rebuilds the simulation and crossfades from the old one, so all four are stepped rather than smoothly swept. The DSP runs its circuit at 192000Hz whatever the patch rate, and loads its triode lookup tables from the plugin's own res folder at start; the binary also names table files for 48000, 96000 and 384000 that the plugin does not ship, but the 192000 path is the one the module selects, so nothing is missing at runtime. The maker's PDF manual was read with pypdf and agrees throughout; it is the source of the account of what the tone stack, Extra Bass and Model do, including the statement that the stack is not flat with the controls centred. The widget adds no context menu of its own.
